text:
jamie: Quick heads up — I flipped FlashAttention v3 on the dedicated-gpu perf rig for Llama-13B (seq=2048, batch=4) and I'm seeing a p99 latency regression compared to v2. Thought I'd put notes here before I dig deeper.

sanjay: Can you paste the numbers and the exact bench command you ran?

jamie: Sure. Baseline (flashattn v2): p50=12.3ms, p95=15.7ms, p99=18.9ms, throughput=220 tok/s.
flashattn v3: p50=11.8ms, p95=17.2ms, p99=28.4ms, throughput=180 tok/s.
Command: ```./bench --model llama-13b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --kernels flashattention_v3 --warmup 50 --iter 200```

marie: ugh that p99 jump is concerning. Any OOMs or kernel fallbacks in logs? Could be extra memcpy or workspace allocation overhead on v3.

jamie: No OOMs. But I saw repeated lines in logs: `flashattn_v3: allocated temporary workspace 256MB` several times per request. v2 seems to reuse a smaller preallocated buffer.

taylor: v3 changed the workspace strategy to trade memory for fewer kernel launches in some cases. For long contexts + small batch it can end up allocating more ephemeral buffers and fragmenting memory — latency hit on tail.

alex: Also check head dim alignment. v3 assumes packed head dims and performs vectorized loads; if our model has padded heads or non-contiguous KV cache layout we might be paying memcpy costs to pack/unpack.

jamie: Good call. Our KV cache uses stride padding for alignment (old optimizer). I can repro with a synthetic shape: head_dim=96 vs 128. With head_dim=96 v3 triggers an internal pack and we see the memcpy.

sanjay: Can we short-circuit by having kernel selection check both kernels on startup and pick the fastest for the workload shape? Add an inline autotune: run 20 warmups for seq buckets and pick winner.

marie: Autotune makes sense but expensive. Maybe fall back to v2 when v3's temporary workspace > threshold or when the model's head_dim % 32 != 0. Also expose env toggles for canary.

jamie: I've added quick switches: ```FLASHATTN_FORCE_V2=1``` and ```FLASHATTN_WORKSPACE_LIMIT_MB=128``` to the bench harness. With FORCE_V2 the p99 goes back to ~19ms. With WORKSPACE_LIMIT_MB=128 v3 falls back to v2 for these shapes and p99 also improves.

ops-bot: Canary deploy started for "flashattn-v3-rollout" on dedicated-gpu (ID: canary-2026-03-20). :rocket:

alex: Two follow-ups — 1) Add a microbenchmark matrix across head_dim x seq_len x batch and store results in telemetry so runtime can make policy decisions. 2) Add a lightweight runtime fallback: try v3, if p99 > baseline+X during warmups, switch to v2 for that route.

taylor: +1. Also log why we fallback (workspace, memcpy, kernel error) so we can triage.

jamie: Action items I'm taking: 1) Add microbench harness and CI job covering head_dim {64,96,128,160}, seq {512,1024,2048}, batch {1,2,4}. 2) Add workspace ceiling env var (already prototyped). 3) Prototype inline autotune with 30 warmups. Will post numbers.

sanjay: Awesome. If you need help instrumenting memory allocs or adding the telemetry schema ping me. :thumbsup:

jamie: Will do. Posting initial PR later today with bench data and a fallback policy draft.

marie: Thanks — really important we avoid silent regressions during rollouts.

jamie: Agreed. I'll include a short note in the rollout playbook about checking p99 on long-context traffic and toggling the env flags.
